children: will be reporting earnings this Monday before market open. Here’s what you need to know.

RadNet beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $622.7 million, up 25% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is RadNet a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting RadNet’s revenue to grow 21.6% year on year, improving from the 13.4% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. RadNet has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at RadNet’s peers in the testing & diagnostics services segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. NeoGenomics delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 11.4%, beating analysts’ expectations by 1.1%, and Guardant Health reported revenues up 36.1%, topping estimates by 2.9%. NeoGenomics’s stock price was unchanged after the resultswhile Guardant Health was down 2.3%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the testing & diagnostics services segment, with share prices up 4.8% on average over the last month. RadNet is up 7% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $94.63 (compared to the current share price of $75.85).
